text:
sam_support: FYI customer hitting streaming hang on Node/edge runtime. They say stream yields first chunk then ReadableStream.read() never returns. Happens when using our TS SDK in Vercel Edge.

maria_customer: repro steps I gave: use @redwood/sdk v1.4.2 (edge build), on Vercel Edge, call client.streamChat(...). Response headers show Content-Type: multipart/x-mixed-replace; boundary=--abc123. After first boundary we get payload then stop. No more data.\nLogs show no socket close or error.\n
sam_support: can you paste minimal code?

maria_customer: 
```
const res = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', messages });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true){ const {value, done} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; console.log('chunk', new TextDecoder().decode(value)); }
```

sam_support: thanks. two quick Qs: what headers do you see exactly (server->client)? and does curl -N reproduce?

maria_customer: headers: 
```
content-type: multipart/x-mixed-replace; boundary=--abc123
transfer-encoding: chunked
connection: keep-alive
```
Curl -N shows the first part and then nothing, same as Node.

lee_devex: tagging @anika_eng — this smells like edge runtime emitting multipart but SDK expecting text/event-stream SSE framing. Could be a boundary format mismatch (we expect boundary without the leading -- in header?).

anika_eng: looking. Two possibilities: 1) model output path accidentally switched to multipart framing for image/mixed responses — SDK streaming parser currently only supports SSE (text/event-stream) and chunked JSON lines. 2) Vercel Edge strips or normalizes boundary token. Need raw TCP capture or curl -v to see exact bytes around boundary. Can you run `curl -v --no-buffer https://...` and paste output?

maria_customer: here's curl -v output (trimmed):
```
> GET /v1/streams/chat HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: multipart/x-mixed-replace; boundary=--abc123
< transfer-encoding: chunked
<
000a
--abc123\r\n
000f
Content-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n
{...}\r\n
0014
--abc123\r\n
```
Then it stops. No final boundary, no further chunks.

anika_eng: aha — our runtime currently writes `--${boundary}\r\n` in front of parts but when setting header we include leading dashes in the header token already (`boundary=--abc123`) so the emitted prefix becomes `----abc123` on the wire, which some clients treat as invalid and stop parsing. Looks like header is double-dashed. That would make many parsers not detect subsequent boundaries. This is a bug in the runtime boundary generation.

sam_support: can we confirm by checking raw bytes for extra dashes? The curl output shows `--abc123` as boundary line which matches header `--abc123` but an extra set could be invisible in some logs. Also why does it send only one part then hang — maybe after mismatch stream parser waits for a delimiter it won't find.

anika_eng: agreed. Short-term workaround: SDK parser can fall back to scanning for `--<token>` even if header has `--<token>` (i.e., tolerate a doubled dash). I'll push a quick patch to dev branch to make streaming parser accept both forms. Also advise customer to set header override in proxy: `boundary=abc123` (no leading dashes) if possible.

lee_devex: I can craft a snippet for customers: if you're using our Edge SDK, set env REDWOOD_STREAM_COMPAT=1 to enable tolerant parsing (we'll add this flag in next patch). For now, use node fetch streaming client (not the edge helper) as a workaround.

maria_customer: would that be safe? we deploy serverless edge and prefer minimal changes.

anika_eng: safe as short-term. Will open ENG-rt-2783 and attach repro and curl output. Priority P1 for Dedicated/hosted customers. Patch plan: runtime will stop adding extra dashes when building boundary token AND SDK will accept tolerant boundaries. Rolling to canary tonight.

deploy-bot: deploy status: canary/eng-runtime v1.3.8 -> rolling out to 5% @ 1976544380 :rocket:

sam_support: thanks. maria — would you be willing to test the canary after deploy? we'll DM with a canary url.

maria_customer: yep I can test, thanks. Appreciate fast turnaround :thumbsup:

anika_eng: adding repro notes: Node/Edge TS SDK v1.4.2, Vercel Edge, payload type: multipart mixed replace, observed on some models when image fragments present. Steps to repro attached. Leaving notes to QA to add unit that parses both `boundary=abc` and `boundary=--abc`.

sam_support: marking this escalated, linking ENG-RT ticket. I'll follow up once canary validated. :white_check_mark:
